The soil here is poor and sandy, so I need to add whatever fertilizer I can get to make the sorghum yield enough food for my family. I was able to get some subsidized NPK from the agro-dealer, and I will also spread cow dung that I collected during the dry season. I am planting the same sorghum seed I saved from last year's harvest because the improved seed is too expensive and hard to find. Since the plot is small and we do not have money to hire workers, my children and I will do all the weeding and harvesting ourselves when the rains come.
